phases.name: Index build
phases.intent: Deterministic ETL from XML/JSON/JSONL into a queryable index. One-shot, cached. No LLM in this phase.
phases.approach: DuckDB with the following normalized tables: filings, registrants, clients, lobbying_activities, lobbyists, lobbyist_roles, contributions, contribution_items, press_releases, members, government_entities, foreign_entities, alis_issues. Source-of-truth fields preserved verbatim (filing_uuid, house_xml_filename, jsonl_line_offset). Loader scripts emit a manifest.json with per-table row counts and source-file hashes for reproducibility.

phases.name: Entity resolution
phases.intent: Build canonical entity IDs across House+Senate registrants, clients, and lobbyists, plus the bioguide_id bridge to press releases.
phases.approach: Three-pass strategy. (1) Bridge keys: Senate registrant.house_registrant_id (already present), House senateID/houseID. (2) Exact-match on uppercased name + ZIP. (3) Fuzzy match (token set ratio >= 92) for the remainder, with a manual-review queue when a single House org has 2+ plausible Senate matches. Result: canonical_registrant_id, canonical_client_id, canonical_lobbyist_id columns on every record.
deliverables: Resolved tables in the DuckDB index
phases.novelty: Most teams will use embedding-based fuzzy matching for everything. We exploit bridge keys deterministically first, only falling back to fuzzy where needed. Faster, cheaper, more defensible.

phases.name: Anomaly surface (Thread 1: open exploration)
phases.intent: Run a battery of deterministic anomaly detectors and rank candidate leads for investigator follow-up.

detectors.name: Spending spikes
detectors.logic: For each (registrant, client, quarter), compute z-score of total income vs. the prior 4 quarters. |z| > 2 surfaces.

detectors.name: Missing-data filings
detectors.logic: Active filings where income/expenses are null AND filing_type is quarterly. Cluster by registrant to find systemic non-reporters.

detectors.name: Revolving door candidates
detectors.logic: Lobbyists with non-empty covered_position. Parse the free text for (a) committee/chamber, (b) member name, (c) role. Cross-join to who their current clients are lobbying.

detectors.name: Foreign-entity flagged filings
detectors.logic: Filings with non-empty foreign_entities[]. Cluster by registrant + jurisdiction. Feeds Thread 2.

detectors.name: Single-client juggernauts
detectors.logic: Registrants with one or two clients but very high income; potential captive lobby shops.

detectors.name: PAC contribution destinations
detectors.logic: Aggregate contribution_items.payee + honoree by registrant and by recipient. Identify recipient members in the press corpus.

detectors.name: Issue-code concentration shifts
detectors.logic: For each general_issue_code, quarter-over-quarter delta in active registrants and total income. Surfacing emerging issues.

detectors.name: New registrant surge
detectors.logic: Registrants whose first filing is in the most recent 2 quarters and whose first-quarter income is in the top 10% of all new registrants.

phases.triage_rule: Each detector outputs a CSV with at most 50 candidates. Investigator agent reads these CSVs, not raw records.
deliverables: data-detective/scripts/query.py with these as built-in templates

phases.name: Foreign influence / FARA gap (Thread 2)
phases.intent: Find lobbying activity for foreign principals that appears in LDA filings but does not appear in FARA (or vice versa). Surface shell-client patterns.
phases.approach: Pull FARA active registrations, normalize names with the same entity resolver, join to LDA foreign_entities[] cluster. Output: (a) FARA-registered foreign principals with no LDA filings, (b) LDA foreign_entities with no matching FARA registration, (c) clients whose name suggests foreign ownership (suffixes like 'Pty Ltd', 'GmbH', non-US PPB country) without foreign_entities[] disclosure.

phases.name: Investigator cycles
phases.intent: Spotlight-style execution. The investigator agent reads ranked candidates from P3+P4, picks the strongest threads, runs follow-up queries via the query layer, and writes findings.json.
phases.novelty: The investigator never reads raw filings during candidate selection. It reads ranked CSVs, requests specific filing_uuids via the query layer, and only loads full record bodies for the leads it has chosen to pursue. This is the corpus-efficiency lever.

phases.name: Fact-check
phases.intent: Verify each high-confidence finding against the source filings AND against external context (FARA, FEC, news reporting). External sources archived via web-archiving skill.
rules: Every claim must cite at least one specific filing_uuid or House XML filename.
Every external source must be archived before citing.
Disputed claims get a resolution path or are downgraded to 'limitation'.

phases.name: Gate 1 — synthesis
phases.intent: Compile findings into evidence-map.json (claim → evidence cards → source records) and findings-report.md. Tom reviews before submission packaging.
exit_criteria: Every claim sourced to a specific record
Each finding has at least 2 independent sources
Evidence map is complete and machine-readable

phases.name: Submission packaging
phases.intent: Package data-detective skill + findings + traces + README per challenge requirements.
validations: All scripts have --help and clear error messages
README maps each finding to the skill invocations and traces that produced it

evidence_card.source_url: string (for filings, the lda.senate.gov public URL; for press, the original URL)
evidence_card.extracted_fields: object (only the fields cited in the claim)

contents.checked_threads: array of thread descriptors with status (open/cold/promising)

guardrails: No claim without an evidence card.
No fuzzy entity matching where a bridge key exists.
No corpus-wide LLM scans. The query layer is the choke point.
Every script must be idempotent and resumable.
All numeric claims (dollars, counts) must be sourced to a specific SQL query with a stable hash.
